questions.question: A catalog must combine governed vocabularies, global IRIs, and named graphs. Which Neptune model is the clearest starting point?
options: RDF queried with SPARQL
Property graph queried only with Gremlin
A reader endpoint with no graph model
An unbounded openCypher traversal
questions.explanation: RDF directly represents subject-predicate-object statements, IRIs, and named graphs, while SPARQL expresses standards-based graph patterns.

questions.question: Why should a fraud traversal start from a bound account ID and name its relationship types?
options: It guarantees every query is served from memory
It bounds the seed set and avoids multiplying unrelated edges at every hop
It creates another storage replica
It converts the graph from property graph to RDF
questions.explanation: A selective starting entity and typed edges constrain the number of candidate paths. Broad seeds and unlabeled hops multiply traversal work.

questions.question: When is Neptune's optional OSGP index most relevant?
options: For reverse traversals that do not bind a predicate or edge label
For promoting a read replica
For enabling continuous backup
For signing requests with IAM
questions.explanation: Without OSGP, reverse traversals across many distinct predicates can require a union scan over POGS. OSGP must be enabled on an empty cluster and has write and storage trade-offs.

questions.question: What must be true for Neptune's S3 bulk loader to read a property-graph dataset?
options: The bucket can be in any Region and anonymous
The loader role needs write access to every bucket in the account
The bucket is in the cluster Region and the associated IAM role can read the objects
The dataset must first be converted to RDF/XML
questions.explanation: The loader reads supported graph formats from an S3 bucket in the same Region and assumes an associated IAM role with the required object access.

questions.question: A writer fails and a cross-AZ Neptune read replica is available. What should the application expect?
options: The replica becomes a second concurrent writer with no interruption
The shared volume is restored from backup before promotion
Neptune promotes a replica, while clients recreate connections and tolerate a brief interruption
Every existing reader connection automatically moves each in-flight query
questions.explanation: A replica can be promoted to the single writer. Existing connections may fail and must be recreated through the cluster endpoint after failover.

questions.question: Why do six storage copies and read replicas not recover an accidental valid delete?
options: Replicas copy the committed delete, so recovery needs a retained restore point
Deletes are stored only on the writer instance
Read replicas never share the cluster volume
Neptune disables automated backups after a delete
questions.explanation: Availability replication preserves committed state, including valid but unwanted changes. Point-in-time recovery restores a new cluster from data retained before the delete.

questions.question: Which signal most directly distinguishes query execution work from time waiting in Neptune's server-side queue?
options: Only the DB cluster name
Slow-query log queryTimeStats such as waitingTimeMs and executionTimeMs
The number of manual snapshots
The VPC subnet count
questions.explanation: Neptune slow-query logs can separate queue waiting, execution, parsing, serialization, and scanned-statement evidence for each slow query.
